content:
In 2024, the U.S. Department of Justice filed a lawsuit against Apple, accusing it of "smartphone monopoly."

Over the past two years, Apple has repeatedly expressed opposition to the case. Now, Bloomberg reports that the Department of Justice and Apple are in discussions to settle the lawsuit.

According to Bloomberg, Apple has put forward "multiple" settlement proposals so far this year:

The report also cautioned that although negotiations are still ongoing, there is no guarantee that Apple and the Department of Justice will ultimately reach an agreement.

The Department of Justice's antitrust lawsuit against Apple mainly centers on five aspects of the iPhone experience: super apps, cloud streaming games, third-party messaging apps, third-party smartwatches, and third-party digital wallets.

Apple has indeed made some substantial changes over the past year in response to some of the Department of Justice's concerns, including supporting RCS in the Messages app, launching a new mini-app partner program on the App Store, and expanding access to the iPhone's NFC chip.

Whether these changes will satisfy the Department of Justice remains to be seen. Of course, political factors are also at play, as Bloomberg noted:

Apple and the Department of Justice recently filed a joint status report on the progress of the case. In addition, Apple also won a dispute earlier this week in the Department of Justice case regarding access to federal government agency documents.

9to5Mac Perspective

If Apple and the Department of Justice ultimately reach a settlement, it would greatly ease the burden on John Ternus, who is set to take over as Apple CEO in September.
